title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods are limited to document-level analysis or narrow token-level tasks, lacking fine-grained localization of arbitrary anomaly types. This paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection and proposes TokenCore, a unified framework that constructs a memory bank of normal token embeddings and uses nearest neighbor matching with max pooling for subword aggregation. TokenCore achieves the best average AUROC across token and document levels on three benchmark datasets, ranking first on Review and Grammar at the token-level.

match_target.why: This is the cheapest single-dataset token-level result that demonstrates the paper's central claim of TokenCore's effectiveness on Grammar errors, requiring only the Grammar dataset and token-level evaluation rather than running all three datasets or document-level aggregation.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: Bounded score (AUROC in [0,1]) on a smaller test set (Grammar has 300 documents, below 2,000 examples). The paper does not report std or CI, so 2.0 absolute points or 0.02 when printed in [0,1] applies.

requirements.stmt: Use BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation for subword-to-word alignment
requirements.quote: All the methods operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation.

requirements.stmt: Construct memory bank M from word-level embeddings of all normal training samples
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank M = {m1, m2, . . . , mN}

requirements.stmt: Aggregate subword embeddings to word-level using element-wise max pooling
requirements.quote: the token-level embedding is computed as: etoken = max(e1, e2, . . . , en)

requirements.stmt: Compute token-level anomaly score as distance to nearest neighbor in memory bank
requirements.quote: we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank: stoken = min_{m∈M} d(etest, m)

requirements.stmt: Aggregate token-level scores to document-level using mean aggregation
requirements.quote: To obtain document-level anomaly scores, we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document. We use mean aggregation: sdoc = 1/T Σ stoken_i

requirements.stmt: Use 50% normal documents as training data, remainder as test set
requirements.quote: We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate using AUROC and AUPRC metrics
requirements.quote: We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Use Euclidean distance as the distance metric for nearest neighbor search
requirements.quote: where d(·, ·) denotes the distance metric (e.g., Euclidean distance).
